subject: Clarification: default storage window for user requests vs generated artifacts
messages:
From: Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@veridianhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Veridian Health Security <security@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Default retention question: do you keep requests or only outputs?

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question as we prep our security questionnaire: your docs say a 45-day default horizon for logs. Can you confirm whether that default applies to raw user inputs (prompts), model outputs (completions), or both? A few specifics we care about:

- Streaming fragments while a session is open (are these persisted before finalization?)
- KV cache / ephemeral context stored for latency (do you persist snapshots?)
- Attachments uploaded to a session (how long are those retained by default?)

I've attached a short sample of the prompt types we send. We need a single-line answer we can include in our security summary and an operational pointer for our engineers.

Thanks,
Nathan Brooks
Sr. Security Engineer
Veridian Health

Attachment: veridian_prompt_examples.txt (text)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Default retention question: do you keep requests or only outputs?

Nathan —

Thanks for the clear examples. Short answer for your security summary: by default we retain both the request (user input) and the model response (finalized completion) for 45 days. Streaming fragments are not kept beyond the session buffer unless they are part of a persisted, finalized record.

A bit more detail to paste into your internal doc or SOC narrative:

- Default horizon: 45 days from creation for stored request/response pairs (applies to hosted API).
- Streaming fragments: transient in-memory buffers during an active session; only the final assembled completion is written to the audit store unless the application explicitly calls an API to persist intermediate fragments.
- KV cache: treated as ephemeral state tied to an active session instance; snapshots are not stored in the long-term audit store by default. If a customer enables persistent caching (opt-in), snapshots will be stored and subject to the same retention window unless configured otherwise.
- Attachments: binary attachments referenced in a request are stored in object storage and follow the same retention policy by default; we provide encryption-at-rest and key rotation controls.

If you need a one-liner: "Default: both user inputs and model outputs are retained for 45 days by default; transient streaming buffers and KV cache are ephemeral unless you opt-in to persistence."

I'll loop Marissa and Karthik in with next steps for a short one-page summary and an appendix we can give to your procurement folks.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@veridianhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Default retention question: do you keep requests or only outputs?

Nathan, Kimberly —

Adding a few operational clarifications and the exceptions table (see attached spreadsheet):

- Edge cases where default retention is different:
  * PCI/PHI workloads: we require a contract addendum; retention can be shortened or extended per agreement and audit controls are applied.
  * Customer-managed private deployment (Private/VPC): retention defaults are controlled by the customer's config; we surface a default of 45 days but infra owners can change the TTL.
  * Debug exports & diagnostic logs: export copies created for customer troubleshooting are marked and retained separately; they inherit the TTL of the export until deletion.

- Practical note on streaming: if your integration uses streaming and records partial transcripts client-side, those client copies are outside our platform retention. Only the server-side finalization is captured by default.

Action items I suggest:
1) We prepare a 1-page "Retention FAQ" you can include in your security packet (we'll include the one-liner Kimberly wrote).
2) If you want proof-of-deletion evidence later (for erasure requests), open a support ticket referencing the JIRA-RET-1427 flow and we can provide deletion runbook artifacts.

I've attached retention_matrix_v2.xlsx with a matrix you can paste into your internal docs.

—Marissa
Sr. Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@veridianhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Default retention question: do you keep requests or only outputs?

Nathan —

Technical follow-up from infra/runtime side so your engineers have clear expectations:

- Persistence path: incoming request payloads are written to the audit store at the end of request processing (after the final token is emitted). We do not persist raw streaming fragments unless the SDK call requests intermediate checkpoint persistence.
- Deletion sweep: a background sweep job runs daily to tombstone records past TTL and a subsequent background compaction/erase job runs weekly for physical removal (we can provide a sanitized excerpt from sweep_runbook.md if you need the timeline).
- Snapshot & cache behavior: KV cache entries are namespaced to a session instance; default ephemeral TTL is the session TTL (minutes). If you enable persistent cache via config, those entries become subject to the 45-day audit TTL.
- Attachments: stored in encrypted object storage; deletion is orchestrated via the same sweep flow but we also flag privacy-sensitive attachments for expedited erasure on request.

I'll drop the sweep runbook excerpt into the support ticket if you open JIRA-RET-1427; that will give you the exact cron windows and retention-confirmation artifacts.

If you'd like, we can schedule a quick 20-minute call with one of our engineers to walk through sample payloads and show how settings change the behavior.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
